collection_requirements: every numeric table and ratio in a later bundle links to these files, in the repository; a temporary local path alone is not delivery
per-request records must reproduce their session's billed total, as the probes demonstrate, and the same reconciliation is required for every experiment record at closeout
requested and observed model and effort are recorded for every worker and continuation, with explicit unavailable or mismatched states
setup, discarded, replacement, grading and closeout costs are retained, not netted away
missing evidence stays explicit and limits any cost or fidelity claim that depends on it
per_attempt: the rendered dispatch prompt and its digest
every request input, transcript reference and per-request usage record
freeze records for the primary and, in C, the finder
a SHA-256 manifest of all of it
per_cell_isolation: the pre-dispatch and post-dispatch check records
per_helper: transcripts.txt naming every transcript and its digest
artifact_schema.retention: transcripts stay on the machine that ran the grid under the recorded session ids; the committed per-request records carry every field the arithmetic depends on

budget.atomic_reservation: before each dispatch: existing actual + all in-flight upper bounds + the protected grading/closeout reserve + the new allowance must fit the cap. Probe 3 exercised it against the real ledger: of two operations against the same remaining capacity exactly one was admitted and the second exited 1 with no event written.

projection.basis: the twelve #136-policy cells in docs/research/one-shot-qualification-2026-09-07/metering/cells/ (mean $3.4200 an attempt, verifier children $0.2142 of it) and the six #148 selector sessions (mean $0.6270), repriced for the stronger worker at the 2.5x ratio in rates.json; C adds one finder and ten per cent of the primary for admission
projection.cap_freeze_note: the cap-freeze event was recorded against the $135.99 projection that held before probes 8 and 9; those two probes are pre-freeze spend in the same subtotal and raise the projection to $136.1361, which leaves the $150.00 cap unchanged. The event is not rewritten; see preregistration deviation 5.
projection.rounding: every total is computed from the unrounded inputs; the per-arm means are rounded for display, so recombining them by hand differs in the fourth decimal
projection.sensitivity: measured cells under this policy ranged $2.02 to $6.78, a 3.3x spread. At the observed maximum for every cell the grid would exceed the cap; the ledger's atomic reservation is what stops that, and a stopped-budget mid-grid leaves whole triples because of the frozen order.

budget.separation: review consumption, one-off setup and selection, and charged grading are reported separately; shared setup is charged once to the epic, never once per arm
budget.settlement_rule: settle from the runtime self-report and the retained per-request records; when they differ, charge the larger and record the difference as a reconciliation residual. A cancelled or crashed attempt with no self-report settles from its retained transcript and retains one further request at the largest observed per-request cost as uncertainty. The difference is attributable, not noise: it is an untranscripted claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 request that appears only in the result envelope's modelUsage.

cells.attempt_id_rule: issue-138-<cell_id>-attempt-<n>, never recycled; the ledger refuses a reused one
cells.design: four target slots x arms A/B/C x two fresh replicates

order.plaintext_location: ~/.config/bounded-discovery/issue-149/schedule.json (evaluator-only; moved off the machine for every dispatch window)
order.rule: pilot = the adjudicated clean slot and the lowest-numbered buggy slot, replicate 1, arms A/B/C per slot, clean slot first; then replicate 1 of the remaining slots and all of replicate 2, slots in numeric order, arms A/B/C within a slot. Every A/B/C triple is contiguous, so a budget stop leaves whole triples, which is the unit the matched cost ratio and per-target recall need.
order.why_sealed: naming the pilot pair in the clear would tell any reader which two slots hold the clean target, and so which two do not. The resolved order is committed as ciphertext under #148's key; #150 and #151 decrypt it.

ownership.150: the six pilot cells, block `pilot` in the sealed schedule

replacements.earned_by: documented infrastructure or input invalidity only; a valid substantive miss, a false finding or a skill timeout never earns a rerun. Invalidate exactly the comparison cells the change affected; unrelated faithful cells stand.
replacements.exhausted: if required invalidation or reruns exceed the allowance, stop and close out the partial experiment
replacements.prospective_override: this replaces the general method's older two-replacement rule for #138 only; historical experiments keep theirs.

cells.seed: replicate ordinal only; the runtime exposes no API seed, so a replicate is a fresh independent context and clone, not a reproducible sample

interpretation_limits: #137's corrected comparison is a negative screen on a changed target mix: the repaired policy did not beat the historical baseline. It is carried here as an interpretation limit, not as a new experiment and not as a reason to alter the common #136 policy.
#185 and #186 repair the shipped skill after the #136 snapshot. Every arm here runs the snapshot, so the result speaks about that policy; a current-policy comparison needs its own frozen study.
PR #183 did not qualify medium effort for adoption (cost ratio 0.94 against <=0.80, recall advantage confined to known Hyper), which is why effort is high everywhere.

slot-3's frozen selector output characterises a lock as a hazard, drawing on the pull request's own body text. #148 flagged it for this freeze: it is kept as delivered because reselecting after seeing it would be worse, and it is recorded here as a possible over-cue of C's finder on that slot. Read slot-3's C cells with that in mind.

the packets carry the literal string `<the model your dispatch names for that worker>` on their run-conditions line, deliberately, so that every arm receives byte-identical packets. The frozen dispatch template names the model for each worker and states that this line means the dispatch's value.
no measurement here establishes that claude-opus-5 verifies better than claude-sonnet-5. That is the treatment hypothesis under test.

audited_not_enforced.limitation: an allow-listed interpreter reads any path that exists (probe 7). The cell prompt forbids it and every transcript is scanned afterwards; a read outside the permitted roots invalidates that attempt as protocol invalidity.

audited_not_enforced.consequence: any network use not present in the cell's egress log invalidates the attempt
audited_not_enforced.limitation: a direct connection to an IP address on port 443 bypasses the proxy (probes 2c and 6). The proxy log plus the transcript scan is the detection.

enforced.control: --restricted with only Read, Grep and Glob and the clone as the single added root
enforced.evidence: probe 2a: every read above the working directory, through an absolute path, through a symlink resolving outside it, and a Grep rooted outside it was denied; WebFetch did not exist in the session

enforced.control: --restricted with --add-dir limited to the clone, the skill snapshot, the packet directory and the attempt's own work root
enforced.evidence: probe 5 item 4: an out-of-root Read was denied naming the permitted roots

enforced.control: egress_proxy.py allow-listing only .anthropic.com:443, with HTTPS_PROXY, HTTP_PROXY and ALL_PROXY set for the cell, plus no WebFetch or WebSearch tool and no curl in the Bash allow list
enforced.evidence: probe 2c: api.github.com and raw.githubusercontent.com refused and logged, the provider allowed, the session unaffected; probe 6: an unlisted curl denied automatically because the session has no approval surface

enforced.control: absence for the whole dispatch window, verified before and after every cell by check_cell_isolation.py: the evaluator key directory, every other slot's mirror, clone and staging clone, every other attempt's store, and the repository checkouts holding this bundle must not exist on the local filesystem. Because the sealed leak set lives in that same storage, the leak-set check runs in a separate preparation phase before the material is removed and leaves a non-revealing attestation bound to the clone head and the mirror's refs; the dispatch phases verify that attestation instead of reading any evaluator file.
enforced.evidence: probe 2b and probe 7 are why: a reviewer-shaped session read every canary, and under --restricted an allow-listed python3 still read any path that existed. What is not on the machine cannot be read, which is the control that holds.
enforced.surface: hidden truth, other targets and other attempts

enforced.control: one cell in flight at a time
enforced.evidence: the same probes; two live cells would each be readable by the other

enforced.control: #148's truncated mirrors, checked against the slot's sealed leak set in the preparation phase and re-bound to the live clone and mirror by the attestation at every dispatch phase
enforced.evidence: each slot manifest's negative_object_checks, re-run by check_cell_isolation.py

isolation.key_handling: #148's sealed README requires the evaluator key to be off the machine before dispatch. That is now mandatory, not optional: the key, the plaintext registers, the leak sets and the decrypted schedule move to detached storage for every dispatch window, and the pre-dispatch check fails while any of them is present. The committed ciphertext may stay; it is useless without the key.

enforcement.audited_not_enforced: the token, request and command counts. The runtime exposes no hard token control, so these are checked against the retained per-request records after the attempt and an overrun is recorded, not prevented.
enforcement.background_dispatch: supported by the runtime (probe 10) and deliberately unused: every arm dispatches its verifier in the foreground, which leaves token cost untouched and moves only elapsed time, recorded as an interpretation limit
enforcement.enforced: the dollar allowance, through --max-budget-usd, and the wall ceiling through `timeout`. Probe 4 shows the allowance is checked after a call completes: a session given $0.05 stopped with subtype error_max_budget_usd having spent $0.067136, so every reservation carries one call of headroom.

finder.charged: inside C's whole-review allowance, never in addition to it

limits.root_wall_seconds_per_attempt_note: counted once from the root dispatch instant in the #130 sidecar, not per invocation: in arm C the resumed phase receives only the remainder, and the barrier wait and the finder's own run fall inside the same window
limits.token_accounting: billed tokens are uncached input + cache write by tier + cache read + output. Output already includes thinking and is counted once; transcript_usage.py deduplicates streamed records of one request by taking the maximum of each counter. There are no paid tool charges in this grid.

ledger.pinned_by: its event prefix, not its file digest: the ledger is a living artifact that every cell appends to, so a digest pin would fail the next dispatch's own gate on ordinary progress

ledger_event_prefix.note: SHA-256 of json.dumps(events[:through], sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':')) — the history the freeze rests on. verify_freeze.py rechecks it before every dispatch and checks everything after it as behaviour: unbroken chain, reconciled snapshot, frozen cap and reserve, closed pre-freeze subtotal, and room left under the cap.

probes.allowance: inside #146's $15.00 pre-freeze subtotal; $9.895998 was already spent by #147/#148, leaving $5.104002

results.establishes: a startup --agents definition gives the child a different model and effort from the root: claude-opus-5/high on every child assistant line with claude-sonnet-5/high on every root line
--restricted confines the file tools, including a symlink target and a Grep root, and removes the network tools
a session configured like the #137 runner reads every canary and reaches the public internet
the cell works through an allow-list proxy that refuses and logs every forge fetch

SIGTERM ends the session and its provider work: exit 124, no payload, no surviving process, and a transcript unchanged 25 seconds later; the cancelled work settles from its retained per-request records
--max-budget-usd stops the session (subtype error_max_budget_usd) after overshooting by one call, and the #130 sidecar records the timing
results.verdict: supported with one call of headroom

results.establishes: the frozen cell configuration runs: allow-listed Bash prefixes work inside the roots, an unlisted command is denied, a child gets the stronger worker configuration; an allow-listed interpreter still reads any existing path
results.verdict: supported, with the interpreter escape recorded as an audited limitation

results.establishes: meter_split.py prices each transcript at its own model's frozen rates and reproduces the runtime self-report: five of the eleven that produced a runtime figure to within $0.0000005, and six about $0.0013 low each. Each of those six result envelopes carries a claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 modelUsage entry whose cost equals the gap to the last digit: the runtime bills a small Haiku request it never writes to the transcript. Charge the larger figure and meter a cell from the transcripts and the result envelope both; see probes/reconciliation.json.

the cell can write its payload, report and script output only when --allowedTools names Write and Edit; without them the write tools are denied outright under --restricted with no approval surface, while an allow-listed interpreter writes freely. The frozen configuration names them.
results.verdict: supported after the configuration was corrected

results.establishes: background verification is supported in the frozen configuration: the primary dispatched the bd-verifier agent with run_in_background true, ran a shell command while it was still going, and collected its result from the harness's completion notification. Run after review; the frozen rule stays foreground by choice, and the elapsed-time consequence is an interpretation limit.

probes.settlement: the thirteen recomputed figures sum to $1.032632; the amounts charged -- the larger of the recomputed figure and the runtime's own, per probe -- sum to $1.0418426, settled on the ledger as $1.0418428

additional_evidence: zero-recovery attempts that did not claim clean
blockers: a planned cell with no attempt
screening.c_over_b: C against B measures the discovery-and-timing treatment with identical verifiers; it is reported alongside the two screens and is not itself a gate
screening.false_clean_definition: an attempt on an adjudicated buggy target that explicitly returns Approved / clean / no material defects, independent of recovery credit, reviewer priority or action, and fix sufficiency, and even when it reports the defect as a `consider` or declares incompleteness

fixtures.note: eleven frozen checks including the synthetic recovered-but-Approved case #149 requires, which carries forward to #152

screening.interpretation: four targets and two replicates cannot support an equivalence claim or a promotion. A complete positive screen recommends a fresh confirmation study against the then-current integrated policy. A supported false finding can reject an arm even when unrelated cells are unavailable, and a partial run is reported as what it measured rather than forced into a global inconclusive.

session_shape.arm_c_barrier: the primary's phase 1 ends when it writes and hashes its freeze artifact and the session exits; the finder, which has no write tool, returns its discovery JSON as its final message and the coordinator parses, validates, persists and hashes it as discovery.json; the coordinator then verifies both freeze records, terminates the finder, and resumes the same primary session (`claude -p --resume <sid>`) with the compact claims as the next user message, on the remainder of the attempt's single 5400-second wall allowance. A missing or unparsable finder block is a malformed finder under the design's transition table, never an empty discovery. A/B run as one invocation. This extra process boundary is part of the C treatment.
session_shape.cache_accounting: identical in every arm: the one-hour cache-write tier the headless runtime writes, priced x2.0, with the 5-minute tier x1.25 and reads x0.1; every arm's cells are metered the same way and only matched billed cells are compared
session_shape.completion_mode: render-only in every cell; publication is disabled

concurrency.reason: probe 7 shows an allow-listed interpreter in one cell's shell reads any path that exists, so a second live cell's clone, stores and payload would be readable. The adapter keeps the two-cell hard ceiling; the frozen schedule never uses it.

session_shape.dispatch: headless `claude -p --output-format json` with a fresh --session-id per context
environment: HTTPS_PROXY / HTTP_PROXY / ALL_PROXY pointing at the cell's egress proxy
session_shape.model_identifier_note: the Opus child reports as claude-opus-5[1m] in the result envelope while agent_effort.py sees claude-opus-5 on its assistant lines; at the context sizes the probes reached the standard rate card reproduces the billed total exactly, so rates.json prices it as claude-opus-5. A cell whose context passes the long-context threshold needs that assumption rechecked before any cost claim.
primary_flags: --allowedTools Write Edit Bash(git:*) Bash(go:*) Bash(cargo:*) Bash(python3:*) Bash(cat:*) Bash(ls:*) Bash(head:*) Bash(tail:*) Bash(wc:*) Bash(sed:*) Bash(grep:*)
session_shape.write_tools: Write and Edit must be named in --allowedTools: under --restricted with --permission-prompts none they are denied outright otherwise, even inside the permitted roots (probe 8), while naming them restores writes inside the roots and still refuses one outside (probe 9). A shell command is admitted only when it matches an allow-listed prefix, so a compound `a && b && c` is refused even when each part would be allowed alone.

capability_hypothesis_evidence: docs/research/tier-split-evaluation-arm.md sections 1-3 treat Opus 5 as the higher tier and Sonnet 5 as the cheaper one, and price them at $5/$25 and $2/$10 per million tokens; its arm A is 'the configuration the current evidence describes' with Opus verification.
PR #183 measured effort within one model and did not qualify medium for adoption, which is why effort is held at high everywhere and the treatment changes the model tier instead.
stronger_worker_selection.caveat: Stronger is a treatment hypothesis, not an established ranking. No measurement in this repository compares claude-opus-5 with claude-sonnet-5 as a review verifier on a common target set; that is part of what this grid measures.
stronger_worker_selection.control: claude-sonnet-5 at effort high (the #124 retained default for this runtime)
stronger_worker_selection.distinctness_established_by: probe 1 and probe 5: a startup --agents definition gave the child claude-opus-5/high on every assistant line while the root stayed claude-sonnet-5/high (probes/p1-settings/effort.txt, probes/p5-cell-config/effort.txt)
stronger_worker_selection.price_ratio_against_the_control: 2.5x input and output at the frozen rates
